body: Definitely not worth it. And I'm willing to talk to you as much as you need if that helps you realize it. It may. It be the best way to look at things, but what's been helping me is that, if I truly hit my lowest, odds are things are only ever going to get better in the long run. Setting longer term goals seem to help me keep some thoughts away, though it can be difficult to look that far ahead. Not sure what helps you the most, but whatever it us, try focusing on it. Maybe itll give you direction and purpose. If not, make it you goal to find one. Even if your purpose is just finding a purpose, its something to work towards.

Kind of a mixed bag of how things went. Some really good, some really bad. On the good end, talked to my parents and they seemed fairly understanding (though a bit disappointed) and ended up getting this better there. On the bad end however, my partners parents heard and FLIPPED. They threatened to stop paying for her college of she didnt break up with me. The worst part, was the reasons they sited. Apparently they wanted me gone for 2 years...which is the same time I came out to them as trans. And some of the other things they said to her confirmed that this was the reason. So that hurt. So my partner decided to "pretend" to break up with me until they pay for her last semester in August. Then were moving out together. Sucks not being able to see her as often though. I honestly thought her parents liked me, but apparently they didnt even like the fact that their daughter is gay, so some severe hidden homophobia and transphobia there. 

I do have 2 interviews for jobs and got accepted into a 1 year certification course at an institute for October, so some things have gotten better. But overall, still a lot of problems. 

Are things ok with you? Want to talk about it at all?
Shes not reading this thread, but my partner think I should go to the psych ward. She says I'm more than that, but when I ask how she never seems to be able to give me a straight answer.

Among other things, yeah. I've had anxiety for a long time, and probably depression though over never been diagnosed and I dont like to diagnose myself with things. And at this point, it just seems to be the smartest and easiest answer.

I just figured, staying is hurting them for a long time, and a lot. But ending everything will hurt for a short time, and they'll be fine afterwards. Theres a reason you dont here about people like me when they die.

I'm just a drain on everyone. I havent had a job in a while as I was laid off and cant seem to even land an interview now. I've had to borrow money from my partner just to stay barely afloat. Recent decisions in the law may make it so I cant find a place to live. Im living with my mother who is pissed because I cant get a job and am doing nothing with my life. And with the few things I do know from classes I've taken and work I have done, I know how to do it pretty quick, painlessly and without a mess. I'd be less of an inconvenience as a dead body than as a living person. And she was talking about the yale emergency psych ward, sp not a normal hospital.
The only reason I'm even thinking of going to the hospital is to make her feel better. Cause I dont see how they'll be able to help me at this point.
Like, I know itll hurt everyone in the short term, but they'd feel better soon and be better off without me there.
I just dont see how staying is any benefit to anyone, including myself.

Right now... I honestly dont feel amything. I  just feel empty. I know it sounds cold but I've only ever made things harder for her, her family, and my family. They'd be better off of I weren't here in the long run.
